title: Completion presentation after a separable residue-field extension
statement: Let $k\subseteq K$ be an extension of fields, let $S$ be a finitely generated $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], let $\mathfrak p\subset S$ be maximal with finite separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] residue field $F=S/\mathfrak p$ over $k$, and let $A=S_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $\widehat A=\varprojlim_r A/(\mathfrak pA)^r$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Fix a $k$-embedding $\iota:F\hookrightarrow K$. Let $\mathfrak q=\ker(S\otimes_kK\to K)$ for the map $s\otimes\lambda\mapsto\bar s\,\lambda$ using $\iota$, put $B=(S\otimes_kK)_{\mathfrak q}$, and let $\widehat B=\varprojlim_r B/(\mathfrak qB)^r$. Fix a $k$-algebra section $\sigma:F\to\widehat A$ of the residue map, let $F$ act on $\widehat A$ through $\sigma$, and fix any continuous $F$-algebra presentation $F[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]\twoheadrightarrow\widehat A$ with kernel $(f_1,\ldots,f_s)\subseteq(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$, equivalently an isomorphism $F[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]/(f_1,\ldots,f_s)\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat A$. Then there is an isomorphism of complete local $K$-algebras $K[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]/(f_1,\ldots,f_s)\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat B$, where coefficients are transported through $\iota$ and the image of every $t_i$ agrees with the image of its chosen element in $\widehat A$. Power series use [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] and algebra tensor products use [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Tag 0C54, lemma-base-change-complete-local-ring, using Tags 0C4Y and 0C50 in its proof.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-separable-point-flat-completion-map] to the given $S,\mathfrak p,K,\iota,\sigma$. It gives the canonical local map $g:A\to B$ and flat completion map $h:R=\widehat A\to C=\widehat B$. The rings $R,C$ are Noetherian complete local, their residue fields are $F,K$, $\mathfrak m_RC=\mathfrak m_C$, and $h\sigma=\tau\iota$ for the structural coefficient section $\tau:K\to C$. These supply all local-ring and coefficient hypotheses below.

source.place: Tag 0C54, local rings, completion map and coefficient square.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-power-series-coefficient-extension-surjection] to $R,C,h$ and the chosen presentation $\phi$. Write $j$ for coefficient extension and $T=K[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]/(j(f_1),\ldots,j(f_s))$. It supplies a surjection $\theta:T\to C$, a local map $\alpha:R\to T$, and $\theta\alpha=h$, with $\theta\pi j=h\phi$. Also $T$ is Noetherian local, $\mathfrak m_RT=\mathfrak m_T$, and the reduced map $T/\mathfrak m_RT\to C/\mathfrak m_RC$ is the identity of $K$.

source.place: Tag 0C54, power-series map, surjectivity and quotient square.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-flat-mod-injective] with its base ring $R$, local algebra $S=T$ through $\alpha$, module $M=C$ through the flat map $h$, module $N=T$, and $u=\theta$. The module $N$ is finite over $T$, generated by $1$. The equation $\theta\alpha=h$ makes $u$ $R$-linear. All local and Noetherian hypotheses hold by Steps 1 and 2, and the reduced map is injective since it is the identity of $K$. Hence $\theta$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 0C54, final paragraph applying Algebra Tag 00ME (lemma-mod-injective).

proof.text: The bijection $\theta$ is a $K$-algebra isomorphism. Its equation $\theta\pi j=h\phi$ preserves every transported series and in particular every chosen variable. A ring isomorphism carries the unique maximal ideal to the unique maximal ideal and hence their powers to each other. It and its inverse are therefore continuous; transporting completeness of $C$ gives completeness of $T$. This is the required isomorphism of complete local $K$-algebras.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0C54, 0C4Y and 0C50, with the final injectivity argument using Algebra Tag 00ME.
